title: Immunometabolic alterations in type 2 diabetes mellitus revealed by single-cell RNA sequencing: insights into subtypes and therapeutic targets.
authors: Li, Huahua; Zou, Lingling; Long, Zhaowei; Zhan, Junkun
one_liner_zh: 该研究利用单细胞RNA测序和机器学习分析T2DM免疫代谢改变，虽涉及转录因子活性分析，但核心是疾病分型与治疗靶点，非蛋白质-DNA互作建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) represents a major global health challenge, marked by chronic hyperglycemia, insulin resistance, and immune system dysfunction. Immune cells, including T cells and monocytes, play a pivotal role in driving systemic inflammation in T2DM; however, the underlying single-cell mechanisms remain inadequately defined. METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from 37 patients with T2DM and 11 healthy controls (HC) was conducted. Immune cell types were identified through clustering analysis, followed by differential expression and pathway analysis. Metabolic heterogeneity within T cell subpopulations was evaluated using Gene Set Variation Analysis (GSVA). Machine learning models were constructed to classify T2DM subtypes based on metabolic signatures, and T-cell-monocyte interactions were explored to assess immune crosstalk. Transcription factor (TF) activity was analyzed, and drug enrichment analysis was performed to identify potential therapeutic targets. RESULTS: In patients with T2DM, a marked increase in monocytes and a decrease in CD4+ T cells were observed, indicating immune dysregulation. Significant metabolic diversity within T cell subpopulations led to the classification of patients with T2DM into three distinct subtypes (A-C), with HC grouped as D. Enhanced intercellular communication, particularly through the MHC-I pathway, was evident in T2DM subtypes. Machine learning models effectively classified T2DM subtypes based on metabolic signatures, achieving an AUC > 0.84. Analysis of TF activity identified pivotal regulators, including NF-kB, STAT3, and FOXO1, associated with immune and metabolic disturbances in T2DM. Drug enrichment analysis highlighted potential therapeutic agents targeting these TFs and related pathways, including Suloctidil, Chlorpropamide, and other compounds modulating inflammatory and metabolic pathways. CONCLUSION: This study underscores significant immunometabolic dysfunction in T2DM, characterized by alterations in immune cell composition, metabolic pathways, and intercellular communication. The identification of critical TFs and the development of drug enrichment profiles highlight the potential for personalized therapeutic strategies, emphasizing the need for integrated immunological and metabolic approaches in T2DM management.
abstract_zh: 背景：2型糖尿病（T2DM）构成一项重大全球健康挑战，其特征为慢性高血糖、胰岛素抵抗和免疫系统功能障碍。免疫细胞，包括T细胞和单核细胞，在驱动T2DM系统性炎症中发挥关键作用；然而，其潜在的单细胞机制仍未得到充分阐明。方法：对37例T2DM患者和11例健康对照（HC）的外周血单核细胞（PBMCs）进行单细胞RNA测序。通过聚类分析鉴定免疫细胞类型，随后进行差异表达和通路分析。利用基因集变异分析（GSVA）评估T细胞亚群内的代谢异质性。基于代谢特征构建机器学习模型以分类T2DM亚型，并探索T细胞-单核细胞相互作用以评估免疫串扰。分析转录因子（TF）活性，并进行药物富集分析以识别潜在治疗靶点。结果：在T2DM患者中，观察到单核细胞显著增加和CD4+ T细胞减少，表明免疫失调。T细胞亚群内显著的代谢多样性导致T2DM患者被分为三个不同亚型（A-C），HC归为D组。T2DM亚型中细胞间通讯增强，尤其通过MHC-I通路。机器学习模型基于代谢特征有效分类T2DM亚型，AUC > 0.84。TF活性分析识别出关键调控因子，包括NF-kB、STAT3和FOXO1，与T2DM的免疫和代谢紊乱相关。药物富集分析突出显示靶向这些TF及相关通路的潜在治疗药物，包括Suloctidil、Chlorpropamide及其他调节炎症和代谢通路的化合物。结论：本研究强调T2DM中显著的免疫代谢功能障碍，其特征为免疫细胞组成、代谢通路和细胞间通讯的改变。关键TF的识别和药物富集谱的开发凸显了个性化治疗策略的潜力，强调在T2DM管理中需要整合免疫学和代谢方法。
